key_idea: Interval stabbing with weighted points: dp[i] = cost when day i is the last visited day, and the previous visited day j must be at least the largest start among exhibitions that end before i, which is a monotone sliding window minimum.
sketch: Let L(i) = max start over intervals with end < i (0 if none), nondecreasing in i. dp[0]=0, dp[i] = c[i] + min(dp[j] for L(i) <= j < i); the answer is the same transition evaluated at a virtual day n+1 with cost 0. Because L is monotone the window only moves right, so a monotonic deque gives O(n+m). Correctness: intervals ending before j are handled by dp[j], intervals with start <= j and end >= j contain j, so only intervals with start > j and end < i could be missed. Use 64-bit sums (up to 2e14). Stress-tested against a bitmask brute force.
